raw.details:
About ELUBuild

ELUBuild is the flagship solo product-building challenge by EduLinkUp. Over the course of the buildathon, individual builders pitch innovative software ideas, and once approved, build, document, and ship real-world SaaS applications from the ground up.

The mission of ELUBuild is to discover and empower solo builders to create sustainable, user-ready digital products. Exceptional projects will be selected for integration into the ELU Store platform, with opportunities for direct deployment, hosting, and potential publishing on the Google Play Store on behalf of EduLinkUp.

The Complete Event Flow

ELUBuild runs across clear, structured phases:

Registration & Track Exploration:

  • Register via the EduLinkUp mobile app.
  • Review the announced tracks and loose problem statement suggestions provided by EduLinkUp. These serve as inspiration-participants are completely free to think beyond these suggestions and tackle any authentic, high-impact problem within the domain.
  • Use this phase to brainstorm, validate needs, and prepare your pitch before the idea portal opens.

Idea Submission Phase:

  • When the idea window opens, submit your idea proposal (project name, problem statement, target users, proposed solution, anticipated tech stack, solo buildability feasibility, and an explanatory video link).
  • You can submit anytime while the window is active.
  • Continuous Review & Approval: The EduLinkUp team reviews submissions on a rolling basis. Ideas can be approved at any time while the window is open.
  • Share Your Vision: Once your idea is approved, you can (and are encouraged to) publish your explanatory pitch video on social media.

Social Media Engagement Leaderboard (Active in Idea & Build Phases):

  • A dedicated engagement leaderboard tracks reach, quality, and engagement of participants' social media posts across both the Idea Phase and the Building Phase.
  • Compelling explanations, progress updates, and demos that resonate with the community rank higher.

Idea Phase Closure, Review & Stage 1 Certification:

  • The idea submission portal closes at 11:59 PM IST on the deadline day.
  • The final review round is completed, and results are officially released to all participants.
  • Stage 1 Certification: All builders whose ideas are approved receive official Stage 1 ELUBuild recognition and advance to the building phase.

Building Phase (Next.js + Supabase):

  • Building takes place inside the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation.
  • Shortlisted builders create their public repository under edulinkup-interns.
  • Mandatory Tech Stack: Projects must be built using Next.js and Supabase, with authentication integrated via EduLinkUp OAuth (@edulinkup/auth SDK). Detailed step by step instructions/guide of connecting your site with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared before the building phase.
  • Weekly Social Updates: Builders must share at least one weekly progress update on social media (e.g., #buildinpublic, feature demos, architecture highlights, or lessons learned). Engaging, authentic content helps you climb the Social Leaderboard.

Repository Commits & Commit Quality Leaderboard:

  • Steady, consistent development through the build window is tracked on a dedicated Commit Leaderboard.
  • Quality & Consistency Over Raw Volume: Scoring evaluates steady engineering rhythm, meaningful commit messages, and genuine code evolution-not artificial commit spamming or scripts.
  • Manual Audits: Code and repository activity will be regularly inspected manually. Use of commit bots, artificial commit scripts, or bulk dumping pre-existing code on the final day will lead to immediate disqualification.

Final Submission & Judging:

  • Submit your GitHub repository (under edulinkup-interns), a deployed live demo URL, and a comprehensive product walkthrough video.
  • Independent evaluations determine top ranks (Winner / Top 1, Top 3, Top 5, Top 7, and All participants).

Event Conclusion, Rewards & ELU Store Integration:

  • Winners and top builders receive trophies, official swags kits, domain vouchers, AI interview vouchers, and certificates.
  • ELU Store Launch: The best app(s) are selected for ecosystem integration into the ELU Store, with maintenance support, live showcase, and potential Google Play Store publication under the EduLinkUp organisation.

Participation & Eligibility

  • Solo Builders Only: Participation is strictly individual. No teams, shared accounts, or outsourced engineering.
  • App-Verified Registration: Registration must be completed via the official EduLinkUp Android app.
  • GitHub Requirement: A valid GitHub profile link must be provided. EduLinkUp issues invitations to the edulinkup-interns organization. Ensure you accept the GitHub organization invite before the build window starts.
  • One Idea Per Participant: Each builder may submit one proposal per edition. Ideas can be edited until the submission window closes.

Idea Proposal Submission Guidelines

Your pitch must address a real-world problem and clearly articulate how it will be delivered solo. Submissions include:

  • Project Name: Clear, brandable name for your product.
  • Problem Statement: Specific, concrete friction point you are solving.
  • Target Users: Exact demographic or professional segment that experiences this problem.
  • Evidence of Need: Why this problem exists and proof that users care.
  • Proposed Solution: Your functional approach and feature roadmap.
  • Anticipated Tech Stack: Confirmation of Next.js, Supabase, and auxiliary APIs/libraries.
  • Solo Buildability Note: Feasibility explanation detailing how the core MVP can be built solo within the build window.
  • Idea Video Link: A public link (YouTube, Loom, Google Drive) explaining your concept clearly in English or Hindi (1-3 minutes).

Note: Ideas are reviewed on merit and feasibility. Clearing this stage qualifies you for the Stage 1 Certificate and unlocks the Building Phase.

Technical & Building Standards

All projects in the building phase must adhere to the following rules:

GitHub Organization: All code must live inside a public repository created in the edulinkup-interns GitHub organisation. Repository ownership remains with the organisation.

Standard Tech Stack:

  • Frontend & Framework: Next.js (App Router recommended).
  • Backend & Database: Individual Supabase project owned and managed by the participant.
  • Authentication: EduLinkUp OAuth using @edulinkup/auth. Detailed step-by-step instructions and guides for connecting your application with EduLinkUp OAuth will be shared with all shortlisted builders prior to the building phase.

Genuine Work Created in Window: All code must be authored during the active build window. Re-submitting existing projects or templates with trivial tweaks is strictly prohibited.

Secret Security: Never commit service-role keys, private API secrets, or database passwords to public repositories. Utilise .env.local and environment variables.

Permitted Resources: Open-source npm packages, public APIs, and AI coding assistants (e.g., Gemini, Copilot, Cursor) are allowed, provided you understand, customize, and own your codebase.

Integrity & Anti-Bot Rule: Commits must reflect authentic engineering progress. Scripted commit bots, fake green-square generators, or plagiarized repos result in immediate disqualification.

Final Submission Checklist

At the conclusion of the build window, participants submit:

  • Repository Link: Working, clean repository in edulinkup-interns.
  • Live Production URL: A fast, functional deployed application (e.g., on Vercel) that judges and visitors can test directly.
  • Demo & Walkthrough Video: Public video demonstrating the end-to-end user workflow, core features, and product value.

Builder Philosophy

ELUBuild is not an academic exercise or a mock hackathon. It is a launchpad to build an authentic, lasting software product that people genuinely use. Build independently. Build publicly. Build something worth keeping.

A solo product-building competition: pitch an idea, and if it is shortlisted, build and ship it in the build window. Each edition has one fixed track and one winner.
